cues.text: Shirts can be cleaned two ways: wash and press, or dry clean. Here is the difference.
Wash and press means the shirt is washed in water with soap, then pressed on a hot shirt machine.
Dry clean means the shirt is cleaned in solvent, not water, and pressed more gently.
Wash and press gives a very crisp finish. Dry cleaning gives a softer finish.
Water is best for sweat. Solvent is best for oil and for delicate fabric.
With wash and press, the customer picks the starch and a hanger or a box. Dry cleaning means less shrinking and fading.
Wash and press costs less. Dry cleaning costs more.
Starch makes a shirt stiff. None is soft, light is a little crisp, medium is crisp, and heavy is very stiff.
Always ask the customer which starch they want, and if they want it on a hanger or in a box.
